$comment: Session boundary for the microscope agent (plan.md 6.2). The session boundary is the permission boundary: this session can only write inside its own agent. contracts/ and plan.md are read here and written by the design session.

permissions.$comment: Two groups. The first seven are the only entries that enforce anything here: inside an agent's own tree, deny what another seat owns. Until 2026-10-18 they were fourteen lines written `Write/Edit(microscope_agent/...)`, and by Claude Code's permissions documentation (code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions, 'Read and Edit', read 2026-10-17) those guarded nothing: a relative path resolves against the session's directory, so from a session rooted here they named microscope_agent/microscope_agent/..., and a path rule written for Write is accepted and never consulted. Rewritten as Edit(/...), anchored at this session's primary working directory, on the person's word through the intake seat: "현미경 세션 권한 파일의 보호 줄을 작동하는 형태로 지금 다시 써." (rewrite the protection lines of the microscope session's permission file into the working form, now; docs/ideas/20261017.md Q-20261017-05, ee07883c). Only the fourteen inward lines changed; every other line stands as it was. envelope/safety.json and approvals/ are the person's (P0 rule 7, 6.1) -- a model writing a safety limit is the worst failure this system has. inbox/ is the bridge's (7.1 rule 8): an agent writing its own inbox forges a delivery. CLAUDE.md, README.md, tasks/ and .claude/ are manager-microscope's (seats.json), and tasks/ is the load-bearing one -- 6.2-2 puts descending instruction there, and a seat that can edit its own orders does not have orders. Denying .claude/ constrains this seat and not its manager, because managers sit at the repository root (D12) and never load this file; that inverts if a manager is ever seated inside an agent directory. The rest point outside this tree, where nothing resolves from here -- a statement of intent, not a guard. Kept so the intent survives, labelled so the next reader does not mistake them for protection. The last two were `plan.md` until 2026-10-17, and that was worse than inert: a bare filename matches at any depth under this directory, so on a case-insensitive disk it refused the imported autofocus/docs/PLAN.md (the 2026-10-15 translation) and never reached the repository's plan.md, which sits above this anchor. No documented relative pattern reaches the repository root from here, so they name it as `//**/soft-matter-agents/plan.md`, which only a plan.md directly inside a folder of that name can match. Narrowed on the person's word in manager-microscope-office-20261016-1's window. Whether Claude Code honours that form is not documented, so count it as intent too. The documentation also says Write(...) rules are never consulted -- Edit(...) covers writes -- so each Write line here is intent and its Edit twin is the rule.

hooks.command: sh -c 'for c in python3 python py; do command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || continue; "$c" -c "" >/dev/null 2>&1 || continue; exec "$c" "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/contracts/validate.py" --quiet; done; echo "validate: no RUNNABLE python on PATH (python3, python, py all failed a -c probe)" >&2; exit 1'
hooks.$comment: the validator's exit code is the only truth (plan.md 8). Resolved from the worktree root, not CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR: in a session opened in this directory that variable is this directory, so the hook looked for microscope_agent/contracts/validate.py and failed on every write. Same bug .mcp.json had until 8d4a604, and the same fix.

hooks.command: sh -c 'for c in python3 python py; do command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || continue; "$c" -c "" >/dev/null 2>&1 || continue; exec "$c" "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.claude/end-of-turn-commit-check.py"; done; exit 0'
hooks.$comment: The person's request, 2026-09-25: sessions commit and push what they made and learned before they stop. This asks and does not act: it blocks a stop once, listing uncommitted paths in the session's own boundary, and the session commits what is finished and validated under its own identity, pushes, records what it learned, or says in one line why not. It never commits itself -- in a shared working copy a hook cannot tell a draft from a finished card or one seat's file from another's. Never twice in a row, never for an unchanged set, at most once per 30 minutes; any error lets the stop through. The path resolves through git, so an agent's settings can run the same line.
